scope: Narrow independent read-only source review of the committed-floor scalar correction; no executed runtime/fault qualification

finding.description: A poisoned typed Log scalar getter could expose the unpublished target floor after a pre-publication error, then reopen at the old acknowledged floor. Store already fenced poisoned wire reads; this concern involved the public typed scalar observer.

resolution_review: A private u64 committed_floor initializes from the validated authoritative manifest.
base_offset/log_start_offset read the committed scalar rather than the staging manifest floor.
publish_floor updates committed_floor only after the first synchronized manifest publication returns success, before cleanup; later cleanup failures keep the durable new scalar.
Errors before successful publication retain the old scalar; an actual publish that is ambiguous can reopen at the same or later floor, never below the last exposed confirmed scalar.
No manifest/data format, path generation, victim authority, retention eligibility, Store actor or wire response contract changes.
The fixed scalar is eight bytes; existing conservative fixed-allocation envelope remains sufficient.
validation_separation: Open_loop retains its failing-first scalar regression and 23 getter/reopen fault scenarios on both toolchains. This receipt does not relabel those executions as independently run.
limitations: Exact pushed corrective source binding is still pending.
Existing Apache component final proof remains exact4ffd and unchanged; it does not qualify local getter behavior.
